This page lists the external software and data standards that wsiTools can
interoperate with. Users should cite both wsiTools and the backends or methods
used in their analysis.

## Citing wsiTools

Until a release DOI is available, cite the exact GitHub release or commit used
for the analysis:

> Caccia, S. *wsiTools: Tools for reading, tiling, converting and exporting
> whole-slide images*. GitHub repository, version `r packageVersion("wsiTools")`.
> <https://github.com/tkcaccia/wsiTools>

Record the package version, commit, operating system, R version, backend
versions, and project files with the analysis. A version number alone is not
enough when the package is installed from the development branch.

The repository also provides machine-readable citation metadata in
[`CITATION.cff`](https://github.com/tkcaccia/wsiTools/blob/main/CITATION.cff),
and the installed R package supports:

```{r, eval=FALSE, purl=FALSE}
citation("wsiTools")
```

No DOI is claimed until a release has been archived by a DOI-issuing service.

## Image access and viewer technologies

- [OpenSeadragon](https://openseadragon.github.io/) is the browser-side tiled
  image viewer.
- [OpenSlide](https://openslide.org/) provides region access to several digital
  pathology WSI formats.
- [libvips](https://www.libvips.org/) provides streaming image operations,
  conversion, and pyramid preparation.
- [Bio-Formats](https://www.openmicroscopy.org/bio-formats/) provides broad
  microscopy-format compatibility and metadata access.
- ZEISS [libCZI](https://github.com/ZEISS/libCZI) is an optional native CZI
  reader when enabled by the local installation.

The exact backend used for each operation should be retained with the project
provenance. Different backends can produce different performance and, for some
formats, different metadata behavior.

## Interoperability and analysis frameworks

- [QuPath](https://qupath.github.io/) is the main interoperability target for
  pathology annotations and GeoJSON round trips.
- [Seurat](https://satijalab.org/seurat/) provides spatial transcriptomics and
  single-cell analysis workflows.
- [Giotto](https://giottosuite.com/) provides spatial-omics analysis tools.
- [SpatialExperiment](https://bioconductor.org/packages/SpatialExperiment/)
  provides a Bioconductor data model for spatial experiments.
- [OME-TIFF](https://ngff.openmicroscopy.org/0.5/) and [OME-NGFF / OME-Zarr](https://ngff.openmicroscopy.org/)
  define interoperable image and multiscale metadata conventions.

## Segmentation and image-analysis methods

When a result uses an external segmentation or preprocessing method, cite that
method separately and report its version and parameters. wsiTools does not
claim ownership of the biological validity of externally generated masks or
predictions.

- [StarDist](https://github.com/stardist/stardist) for optional star-convex
  object segmentation.
- [DeepCell Mesmer](https://deepcell.readthedocs.io/en/master/app-gallery/mesmer.html)
  for optional multiplex/DAPI segmentation workflows.
- [Nature Methods computational-methods guidance](https://www.nature.com/articles/nmeth.3686)
  for reporting software, test data, parameters, and reproducibility.

## Data and provenance

For every published example, provide the source or accession for the slide,
spatial object, annotation, and segmentation files. If data cannot be shared,
state the restriction and provide a small synthetic or de-identified fixture
that exercises the same workflow.

At minimum, record:

- input file checksums or immutable accessions;
- scanner and file format where known;
- spatial-object version and image/section identifier;
- annotation and registration transforms;
- backend and package versions;
- random seeds and model parameters;
- output project and measurement files.
